review_comments.body: I'm curious about the decision to use 3 spaces between the cast and macro name in these PRs. Is there any reasoning behind it, or is it just arbitrary?
It's to align to the next tab
which... in this case is wrong :D
(I'll check the indentations because I've done a lot of C/C xD)
Cool. WDYM by align to the next tab? The indentation in the next function body? (Sorry if that's a silly question, it's late for me.)

Oh no, it's not a silly question. You see, when I define multiple macros, or when I use imports, I do

```C
#include <...>			// XXX
#include <.........> 	// YYY
```

where `//` are aligned vertically. To ease alignment, I don't use spaces but only tabs after `>`. That way, it's always on a multiple of 4 that `/` is placed. Same for macros:

```C
#define NAME			WHAT1
#define NAME........	WHAT2
```

Generally those macros do the same work and thus it's always in prevision of future similar macros. It's also a bit easier to read the macro body when it's not stick to the macro declaration, e.g.:

```C
#define DO_SOMETHING_(op) ((PTR *)(op))
```

vs

```C
#define DO_SOMETHING_(op)	((PTR *)(op))
```

Ah, got it. Thanks for clarifying! This is why we invented formatters, though :smile:

> It's also a bit easier to read the macro body when it's not stick to the macro declaration

I actually see the opposite! For me, the second one here takes an extra second to process. I don't think it matters much for your fleet of PRs, though--I was just curious. (But you should probably aim for <=4 when there's just one macro.)

> I don't think it matters much for your fleet of PRs

And this is only the first wave! Fixing all UBSan failures is a really really long process and at the end, we need to fix Clinic as well (which I still don't know how to do it properly...)
What's broken with clinic? I can probably take a stab at it. (I've fixed two issues with it before.)
I've tagged you on the issue (https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/128180).
Will take a look tomorrow (unless I'm asleep all day, otherwise I'll look at it on Saturday).
